events.text: The first lesson is on the edge of your isle, where the cloud falls away. {npc} looks down once, then stops looking, and asks you to begin.

choices.text: Teach {him} to stand on the wind first

effects.log: By evening {npc} can stand a hand above the cloud, shaking and delighted. You do not tell {him} how long it took you.

mem.note: taught me to stand on the wind

choices.text: Teach {him} to breathe the thin air

effects.log: You sit facing each other while the stars come out below you. {npc} breathes the way you do by the end of it.

mem.note: taught me to breathe above the clouds

events.text: {npc} comes to the lesson with a list: every question {he} has been saving since the wedding. Most of them are about the arts. Some are about you.

effects.log: It takes until moonrise. {npc} folds the list away, all of it crossed out but one, and does not tell you which.

mem.note: answered every question on my list

choices.text: Answer only the ones about the arts

effects.log: {npc} notices which ones you skipped, and smiles, and keeps them for later.

mem.note: kept some answers back

events.text: {npc} has watched you train on the terrace since {he} could walk. Today you put a practice sword of cloud-wood in {his} hands and step back.

choices.text: Show {him} the form you never show anyone

effects.log: {npc} learns it the way you did, badly and then all at once. {He} does not ask why today.

mem.note: showed me the form they kept for themselves

choices.text: Spar at an immortal's full speed

effects.log: You do not hold back, quite. {npc} ends the morning on {his} back on the cloud, laughing.

mem.note: sparred with me for real at last

events.text: A grown child of the isles does not take a lesson the way a small one does. {npc} questions every correction, tries it {his} own way, and falls through a cloud twice before trying yours.

effects.log: On the third fall {npc} finds it, and looks up at you from the cloud, and you nod.

mem.note: let me find my own mistake

choices.text: Catch {him} and correct it at once

effects.log: {npc} bristles, then does it right, and later says it was the right thing.

mem.note: caught me and corrected me

events.text: You unroll the scroll of the art for {npc} on a table of white jade. {He} reads the first line and looks up. "Who else knows this?"

effects.log: {npc} reads the rest in silence and rolls it up very carefully, as if it might break.

mem.note: gave me an art no immortal has

choices.text: "Only the ones I would die for"

effects.log: {npc} is quiet for a long while. Then {he} gives the scroll back and asks you to show {him} instead.

mem.note: told me who an art is for

events.text: The first art you pass to {npc} is the one that brought you up the white stairs. {He} learns the shape of it in a season, and then asks what it cost you.

effects.log: You tell {him}, all of it. {npc} practises the art differently afterwards: more carefully, and not more slowly.

mem.note: told me what the art cost them

effects.log: {npc} looks at you a moment too long, and then goes back to practising.

mem.note: said the art was worth it

events.text: By the end of the season {npc} has the art, and the next morning there is a crane at your window with a message: a faction elder wants to know where {he} learned it.

choices.text: Tell the elder it is a family art

effects.log: The crane flies back. The isles learn your house has an art of its own, and they treat {npc} more carefully.

mem.note: told the factions the art was ours

effects.log: Silence is an answer too. {npc} keeps the art, and nobody asks again.

mem.note: kept my art out of the factions' hands

events.text: {npc} breaks through on a quiet morning, and you feel it from across the isle: a realm above your own. {He} comes to find you, and does not know what to say.

effects.log: You bow as an immortal bows to a senior, sleeve to the cloud. {npc} goes scarlet and pulls you upright by both hands.

mem.note: bowed to me when I passed them

effects.log: {npc} looks at you as if you had given {him} the whole isle.

mem.note: asked me to teach them back

events.text: The isles talk about {npc} now, not about you: a realm above the one who taught {him}, and young for it.

effects.log: You tell every wine house on the isle. {npc} is mortified and very pleased.

mem.note: told the isles I had passed them

effects.log: You say nothing. {npc} notices you on the terrace before dawn every day after, and understands.

mem.note: started training harder when I passed them

events.text: The red thread is cut before witnesses of the Jade Court. {npc} stands at the edge of your isle with one sleeve of belongings, waiting for a skiff.

effects.log: You press a heavy pouch of stones into {his} hand. {npc} weighs it once and does not thank you. You did not expect {him} to.

mem.note: gave me half the stones at the edge of the isle

effects.log: {npc} studies your face as the skiff comes in. "So am I," {he} says, and steps aboard.

mem.note: said sorry at the edge of the isle

events.text: {npc} takes down the cloud-silk hanging {he} brought to the wedding and folds it small. "Keep the pavilion," {he} says. "I will not want to see it from above."

effects.log: {npc} hesitates, then hangs it back. "For the pavilion," {he} says. "Not for you."

mem.note: asked me to leave the hanging

choices.text: Help {him} carry it to the skiff

effects.log: You carry it together in silence. It is the kindest hour of the last year.

mem.note: helped me carry my things to the skiff

events.text: {npc} finds you on the terrace at dusk. "Was it me?" {he} asks. "The thread. Was it because of me?"

effects.log: You tell {npc} everything, slowly, while the isles go dark below. {He} is angry, and then quiet, and at the end {he} leans on your shoulder.

mem.note: told me the truth about the red thread

effects.log: {npc} lets out a breath {he} has been holding for a year.

mem.note: told me it was never me

events.text: A year after the red thread was cut, {npc} still crosses to the other isle every new moon to see {his} other parent. Today {he} asks you to come too.

effects.log: It is stiff and polite and short. {npc} holds both your hands on the way back.

mem.note: came with me to the other isle

effects.log: {npc} carries the gift across. It is something.

mem.note: sent a gift across the cloud

events.text: Decades later you meet {npc} on a bridge of the Lantern Guild. {He} looks well. {He} has seen you first.

choices.text: Ask how {he} has been, and mean it

effects.log: You stand on the bridge until the Guild lights its lanterns, trading news of a century. You part as two people who were once one household, and are glad of it.

mem.note: asked after me on the bridge, and meant it

effects.log: {npc} nods back. The bridge is long enough for both of you.

mem.note: nodded on the bridge and walked on

events.text: At a banquet of the Eight Houses you are seated, by some steward's cruelty or joke, beside {npc}.

effects.log: By the third course you are both laughing at the steward. It is a good evening, against all odds.

mem.note: made the best of the banquet with me

effects.log: You change seats. {npc} looks relieved, and a little hurt.

mem.note: changed seats rather than sit with me

events.text: The isles are whispering about you and {npc}: a master and a student. Today a faction lady stops you on a bridge to say so, loudly.

choices.text: Walk past with {npc}'s hand in yours

effects.log: You walk the bridge together, slowly, past every faction balcony. By the far end the whispers have become mostly about how brazen you are.

mem.note: held my hand on the bridge, openly

effects.log: The lady goes red. The isles have a new story by evening, and it is not about {npc}.

mem.note: answered the whispers for me

events.text: {npc} has heard what the isles say, and comes to you pale. "If it costs you your name," {he} says, "I would rather go."

choices.text: Tell {him} the name is not worth it

effects.log: {npc} stays. In a decade the isles have other stories, and you still have each other.

mem.note: said their name was not worth losing me

effects.log: {npc} waits. It is a long season for both of you.

mem.note: asked me to wait a season

events.text: A month after, {npc} brings you cloud-tea on the terrace as if nothing had been said. {His} hands shake a little on the cup.

choices.text: Take the tea, and never speak of it

effects.log: You drink the cloud-tea. Neither of you mentions it again, and the terrace slowly forgets it too.

mem.note: never spoke of it again

effects.log: {npc} sets the pot down very carefully. "Then we can go on," {he} says.

mem.note: apologised properly

events.text: {npc} has asked to train with another master on another isle. {He} says it is for the arts. {He} does not look at you when {he} says it.

effects.log: {npc} bows lower than {he} ever has, and goes. {He} writes every season.

mem.note: let me go with their blessing

choices.text: Ask {him} to stay as your student

effects.log: {npc} stays. The terrace is quieter than it was, and kinder.

mem.note: asked me to stay a student

events.text: You teach {npc} the first thing a god learns: to hear one prayer among ten thousand. {He} sits beside you in the domain's quiet and tries.

choices.text: Guide {his} hearing to a small world

effects.log: At dusk {npc} hears it: a child in a small world, asking for rain. {He} turns to you, astonished.

mem.note: taught me to hear one prayer

choices.text: Let {him} drown in all of them first

effects.log: {npc} hears every prayer at once and weeps, and then, slowly, learns to choose.

mem.note: let me hear every prayer first

events.text: {npc} wants to learn to make something, not to fight. You give {him} a handful of the first riverbank's clay and an age.

choices.text: Teach {him} to give the clay a breath

effects.log: By the end of the age a small clay bird sits on {npc}'s palm, breathing. {He} will not let anyone else hold it.

mem.note: taught me to give clay a breath

choices.text: Teach {him} to let it be clay

effects.log: {npc} is disappointed, then thoughtful, then grateful.

mem.note: taught me to let things be what they are

events.text: {npc}, god-touched since birth, asks for the lesson you have put off for an age: how to hold a domain without being held by it.

choices.text: Give {him} a corner of your domain to keep

effects.log: {npc} keeps it for a century. It grows strange and lovely, and entirely {his}.

mem.note: gave me a corner of their domain to keep

choices.text: Show {him} how you nearly lost yours

effects.log: You show {him} the scar in your domain. {npc} looks at it a long time and does not ask anything else.

mem.note: showed me where they nearly lost their domain

events.text: {npc} spars with you at the border of the War Domain, and holds nothing back, and is better than you thought.

effects.log: The War Domain's gods stop to watch. {npc} loses, and grins at you through the dust of stars.

mem.note: sparred with me at the border of war

choices.text: Stop and teach the one thing {he} lacks

effects.log: {npc} learns it in a single exchange and is a different fighter after.

mem.note: stopped to teach me the one thing I lacked

events.text: You give {npc} the art the way gods do: by dreaming it into {him}. {He} wakes knowing it, and comes to find you.

choices.text: "It was always going to be yours"

effects.log: {npc} holds your hands for a long moment. The art sits in {him} like a second heart.

mem.note: said the art was always mine

effects.log: {npc} promises. A god's promise is a heavy thing, and {he} carries it well.

mem.note: asked me to use the art for the worlds

events.text: {npc} uses the art you gave {him} for the first time to save a world that was not praying to anyone.

choices.text: Tell {him} that was the right use

effects.log: {npc} glows, which a god can do, and the saved world calls it a second sun.

mem.note: told me I used the art rightly

choices.text: Warn {him} that the world will want more

effects.log: {npc} listens. When that world starts praying, {he} answers wisely.

mem.note: warned me what a saved world wants

events.text: A pantheon sends an envoy: the art you gave {npc} belongs, they say, to a god of theirs who died an age ago.

choices.text: Tell the envoy whose it is now

effects.log: The envoy goes home. The pantheons learn your house keeps what it teaches.

mem.note: stood between me and the pantheon

choices.text: Offer the pantheon a gift for its dead

effects.log: The pantheon takes the gift and the matter ends, gracefully.

mem.note: paid the pantheon for my art

events.text: {npc} rises a step of godhood past you, and the domains feel it before you do. {He} comes to you first, before any pantheon can.

effects.log: You kneel. {npc} pulls you up at once and holds on.

mem.note: knelt to me, laughing

effects.log: {npc} tells you. Some of it you will see yourself, one day.

mem.note: asked what I could see from above them

events.text: The pantheons court {npc} now: a god above the one who taught {him}. Three envoys wait at your border for {his} answer.

effects.log: {npc} chooses. Whichever it is, {he} chose it.

mem.note: let me choose my own pantheon

effects.log: You sit together through an age of deciding. It is the best age you have had.

mem.note: sat with me while I decided

events.text: The vow is unwoven before the Court of Vows. {npc} gathers the worlds that prayed to you both and divides them, carefully, like a meal.

effects.log: {npc} notices, and says nothing, and takes the better half. It is the last gift of the vow.

mem.note: gave me the better half of our worlds

effects.log: {npc} is silent for an age, or a breath. "Gods are rarely sorry," {he} says, and is gone between the stars.

mem.note: said sorry before the Court of Vows

events.text: Your shared temple must have one god now. {npc} stands in its doorway, and the worshippers inside are very quiet.

effects.log: {npc} bows and takes it. The worshippers do not know which of you to thank.

mem.note: gave me our temple

choices.text: Leave it empty, for both of you

effects.log: The temple stands empty. Both of you visit it, never at the same time.

mem.note: left our temple to nobody

events.text: {npc} comes to you in a dream, which god-touched children can. "The vow," {he} asks. "Did it break because of me?"

effects.log: {npc} listens to all of it inside the dream. When {he} wakes, {he} lights a lamp at your altar for the first time in a year.

mem.note: told me the truth about the vow

effects.log: {npc} wakes lighter. You can feel it from your domain.

mem.note: told me it was never me

events.text: {npc} keeps two altars now, one for each parent, and asks if you mind which one {he} lights first.

choices.text: Tell {him} to light the other first

effects.log: {npc} lights it, and then yours, and you feel both flames.

mem.note: told me to light the other altar first

choices.text: Tell {him} the truth: you mind a little

effects.log: {npc} laughs, and lights both at once.

mem.note: told me the truth about the altars

events.text: An age later, at the Feast of Domains, {npc} is across the hall. {He} raises a cup to you before you can look away.

effects.log: You talk until the servants of the feast clear the last cups. When you part, the hall has forgotten to watch you.

mem.note: crossed the feast hall to speak with me

choices.text: Raise your cup back, and stay

effects.log: {npc} nods. The feast is long enough for both of you.

mem.note: raised a cup from across the hall

events.text: A world prays to you and to {npc} together, not knowing the vow is unwoven. Its prayer reaches you both at once.

choices.text: Answer it together, one last time

effects.log: You answer together. The world is saved, and never learns anything changed.

mem.note: answered a prayer with me one last time

effects.log: {npc} answers it alone. Somehow you are both grateful.

mem.note: left the prayer to me

events.text: The pantheons are whispering: a god and one they taught. At the Feast of Domains an elder god says it aloud, to the whole hall.

choices.text: Take {npc}'s hand in front of the hall

effects.log: The hall goes quiet, then goes back to its wine. Something has changed in how they say your names.

mem.note: held my hand before the pantheons

effects.log: The elder god goes very still. The pantheons have a new story by morning, and it is not about {npc}.

mem.note: answered the elder god for me

events.text: {npc} has heard what the pantheons say. "If it costs you a domain," {he} says, "I would rather go back to being your student."

choices.text: Tell {him} no domain is worth it

effects.log: {npc} stays. In an age the pantheons have other stories, and you still have each other.

mem.note: said no domain was worth losing me

effects.log: {npc} waits. It is a long age for both of you.

mem.note: asked me to wait an age

events.text: An age after, {npc} brings you nectar at the edge of your domain as if nothing had been said. The cup trembles, very slightly.

choices.text: Take the nectar, and never speak of it

effects.log: You drink the nectar. In an age the domain has grown over the moment, as domains do.

mem.note: never spoke of it again

effects.log: {npc} bows, as {he} did the first day. "Then I will keep bringing the nectar," {he} says.

mem.note: apologised properly

events.text: {npc} has asked a pantheon to take {him} as a student. {He} says it is for the arts. {He} says it in a dream, so {he} does not have to see your face.

effects.log: {npc} goes. Every age a small prayer arrives from {him}, just to say {he} is well.

mem.note: let me go with their blessing

effects.log: {npc} stays. Your domain is quieter than it was, and kinder.

mem.note: asked me to stay a student

events.text: {npc} has learned the art you gave {him}, and uses it the first time to catch a falling crane-chick before it drops through the cloud.

choices.text: Tell {him} that is what it is for

effects.log: {npc} sets the chick back in its nest and keeps the moment like a jewel.

mem.note: said the art was for catching what falls

choices.text: Tease {him} for using it on a bird

effects.log: {npc} laughs, and uses it on you next, gently, to prove a point.

mem.note: teased me about the crane-chick

events.text: The Red Thread Elder asks you both, as the rite demands, whether anything is owed. {npc} looks at you and waits.

effects.log: You say it. {npc}'s eyes fill. "Yes," {he} says. "The years."

mem.note: said we owed each other the years

effects.log: The Elder writes "nothing". {npc} signs under it with a steady hand.

mem.note: said nothing was owed

events.text: {npc} sends you a crane after a century: {he} has married again, on a far isle, and wanted you to hear it first.

effects.log: You send a jar of thousand-year cloud-wine. A crane comes back with one word: "Thank you."

mem.note: sent a gift for my second wedding

effects.log: The crane goes back with nothing. {npc} understands that too.

mem.note: sent the crane back empty

events.text: The isles have noticed the distance between you and {npc} at the lessons. A faction elder asks {npc}, loudly, whether {his} master has been unkind.

effects.log: You say it was your fault, and only yours. {npc} looks at you with something like gratitude.

mem.note: took the blame before the elder

effects.log: {npc} says "My master is kind." It is the bravest thing you have heard {him} say.

mem.note: let me answer for myself

events.text: A year on, {npc} breaks through a realm under your teaching, and comes to tell you before anyone else, as a student does.

effects.log: You do it properly, and nothing more. {npc} bows, relieved and proud.

mem.note: congratulated me as a master should

choices.text: Give {him} a gift worthy of the realm

effects.log: {npc} takes it with both hands. "From my master," {he} says, carefully.

mem.note: gave me a gift for my realm

events.text: A teller in a wine house of the Lantern Guild has made a song about you and {npc}. It is unkind, and very catchy.

effects.log: You pay the teller to stop singing it, and to teach you the second verse.

mem.note: bought the song about us

effects.log: You sing it with {npc} in the next wine house. By the end the isles are singing along.

mem.note: sang the song about us, louder

events.text: A crane brings news to the Jade Court: {npc} has passed you. The ministers look at you sideways for a week.

effects.log: You fill the pavilion for {npc}. {He} says it is too much and enjoys every hour.

mem.note: held a banquet when I passed them

effects.log: You train under {npc} for a season, and the isles stop looking sideways.

mem.note: asked me to train them

events.text: {npc} uses the art you gave {him} to mend a crack in your domain that you had stopped noticing.

effects.log: {npc} only says the crack was bothering {him}. It was not; it was bothering you.

mem.note: thanked me for mending the crack

effects.log: "I look at your domain more than you do," {npc} says.

mem.note: asked how I saw the crack

events.text: Your shared pantheon must decide which of you keeps its seat. Its elders look from {npc} to you.

effects.log: {npc} takes the seat and bows to you from it, once.

mem.note: gave me the pantheon's seat

effects.log: You keep it. {npc} leaves the hall without looking back.

mem.note: kept the pantheon's seat

events.text: An age on, {npc} sends a dream to your domain: {his} new consort, a god of a far pantheon, and a small request to be happy for {him}.

effects.log: You send one. It arrives as rain on {npc}'s wedding.

mem.note: blessed my second wedding

effects.log: You wake. {npc} understands that too.

mem.note: woke from my dream

events.text: The pantheons whisper that {npc} no longer brings you prayers to answer. An elder god asks you why.

effects.log: You say it, plainly. The elder god nods, and the whispering moves on to someone else.

mem.note: took the blame before the pantheons

effects.log: {npc} hears of your silence and starts bringing the prayers again.

mem.note: kept silent about it

events.text: An age on, {npc} rises a step of godhood under your teaching, and comes to you first.

choices.text: Bless the step, as a teacher

effects.log: You bless it, and nothing more. {npc} bows, relieved.

mem.note: blessed my step as a teacher

effects.log: {npc} takes the small world into both hands. "From my teacher," {he} says, carefully.

mem.note: gave me a world to keep

events.text: A world below has made a festival of you and {npc}: a god and the one they taught. Its priests are not sure it is allowed.

effects.log: You send fair weather. The festival becomes a custom.

mem.note: blessed the festival of us

choices.text: Send the priests a dream to stop it

effects.log: The festival stops. {npc} is quietly sorry about it.

mem.note: stopped the festival of us

events.text: The Book of Fates moves your consort {npc}'s line above yours. The clerks of the Court read it aloud, as the law requires.

effects.log: You stand in the Court and applaud alone until others join. {npc} hides {his} face.

mem.note: stood and applauded in the Court

choices.text: Ask {him} for a lesson that same night

effects.log: {npc} teaches you until dawn, and is a very strict teacher.

mem.note: asked me for a lesson that night
